key_insight: Matrix product states let adaptive non-local observable quantum super-resolution circuits be simulated far beyond statevector limits while preserving near-exact accuracy at modest bond dimension.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical scalable backend for benchmarking and training large quantum image super-resolution models on a single GPU.
method: Built an MPS simulator for ANO-VQC forward feature extraction
Compared scaling against statevector and exact tensor-network contraction
Swept bond dimension across circuit depths and trained Fashion-MNIST SR models
evidence_signal: On one RTX 4070, MPS handled inputs up to 16×16 (256 qubits), while statevector failed at 6×6 and exact TN became impractical beyond 12×12; near-exact bond dimension rose from chi=2 at L=1 to chi=16 at L=4.
watch_item: The reported scalability and quality are shown under shallow-circuit settings, so deeper circuits may require substantially larger bond dimensions and higher compute cost.
paper_title: Scaling Adaptive Non-Local Observable Quantum Super-Resolution via Matrix Product States
